NoteThe Brief




Explore barriers to harmonisation of RADB and eData exposure data format
Compare existing vocabulary (both in format and practice) used in RADB
Develop recommendations for prioritisation based on anticipated needs
This site contains exploration of and recommendations for harmonisations of RADB’s environmental_con table (and dependent tables) with eData’s format. I have reviewed both controlled vocabulary tables and the actual data in RADB and developed a set of recommendations. Each table column or group of columns is also assigned a priority and difficulty score /5. Depending on the planned use of the format in future (e.g. our discussion around using eData for particle-based stressors), these scores may change, but I have assumed that use will continue to focus largely on conventional chemical stressors in water.
Tables below summarise my recommendations and score - click on a variable in the left-hand column for a more detailed exploration. So far I have focused on what I believe are the main tables:
